hypothesis: Each SLOAD in OverlayStateProvider::storage_from_db opens and drops a fresh HashedStorages dup cursor (cursor_with_dbi + Arc clone + mdbx_cursor_open/close under the txn mutex), ~10% of heavy-phase server CPU in base-symbols. Caching one cursor per provider removes that per-slot cost; the B-tree seek itself is unchanged. Expect heavy eth_call ~8-10% faster (~3-5% total), light unchanged.
llm_commentary: Reusing one HashedStorages/PlainStorageState dup cursor per OverlayStateProvider (instead of opening and dropping one per SLOAD) cut wall time 4.9% on c8a (5.36→5.10s), 5.3% on c8i (7.17→6.79s) and 6.6% on c8g (8.90→8.31s), with no run overlapping its baseline's range. That is at the top of the 3-5% total predicted from base-symbols, where cursor_with_dbi + Arc clone + mdbx_cursor_open/close under the txn mutex was ~10% of heavy-phase server CPU and the heavy phase is ~57% of wall time. The light phase (one SLOAD per call) should be unaffected, so the whole gain is heavy calls getting ~9-11% cheaper; Graviton gains most, consistent with costlier atomics/mutex on the per-cursor path. Remaining heavy-path costs are the MDBX seek itself (~19%), keccak of address+slot per SLOAD (~19% incl. the contract's own), the txn_execute mutex per get, and the per-SLOAD cached_storage_settings RwLock read; next is the compiler rung (maxperf, znver5 on c8a), then PGO.
